extracted.intended_audience: general public and prospective NEH applicants (institutions and individual scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the National Endowment for the Humanities' purposes, program/division priorities, award criteria, and procedural review elements that guide which humanities projects the agency funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support high-quality humanities projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The NEH provides grants for high-quality humanities projects to cultural institutions such as museums, archives, libraries, colleges, universities, public television, and radio stations, and to individual scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH's mission: 'promoting excellence in the humanities and conveying the lessons of history to all Americans.' Examples of funded project types appear across the article (exhibitions, documentaries, digital history, digitization/transcription projects, conferences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award grants that strengthen teaching and learning in the humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: One stated purpose of NEH is awarding grants that strengthen teaching and learning in the humanities in schools and colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This priority aligns with the Division of Education and with NEH-supported resources for teachers and students (e.g., EDSITEment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate research and original scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH seeks to facilitate research and original scholarship in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Division of Research 'makes awards to support the publication of books in and outside the humanities.' This priority supports scholarly publications and original research projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide opportunities for lifelong learning
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH aims to provide opportunities for lifelong learning in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-facing programs and resources (magazine, public programs division, EDSITEment) are examples of supporting lifelong learning beyond formal education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and provide access to cultural and educational resources
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH awards grants to preserve, maintain, and improve access to primary sources in the humanities, in both digital and analog form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division of Preservation and Access administers these grants. Notable funded projects include large newspaper microfilming/digitization efforts (United States Newspaper Project → Chronicling America) and 'What's on the Menu' community-sourced transcription/digitization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen the institutional base of the humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH supports strengthening the institutional base of the humanities, including capacity building for humanities institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically the Office of Challenge Grants administered capacity-building grants and encouraged fundraising; similar programs now live in the Division of Preservation and Access. This priority can include institutional development and sustainability activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients: cultural institutions and individual scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH grants are directed to cultural institutions (museums, archives, libraries, colleges, universities, public TV/radio) and to individual scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH also supports a network of 56 state and territorial humanities councils as part of its federal/state partnership; eligibility and program fit depend on the division or initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review and National Council-informed decisionmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The NEH chair's grant and award decisions are informed by recommendations from the National Council on the Humanities, peer-reviewers selected to read each project proposal, and the Endowment's staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The National Council is a board of (about) 26–27 appointed private citizens with expertise; peer reviewers are selected to read each proposal. This indicates NEH uses peer review and council recommendation as primary evaluative procedures for grant decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division: Division of Preservation and Access priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: This division 'awards grants to preserve, maintain, and improve access to primary sources in the humanities, in both digital and analog form.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects improving access to primary-source collections, digitization, restoration, archival preservation, and infrastructure for access are in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division: Division of Public Programs priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Public Programs supports projects that bring the humanities to large audiences through libraries and museums, television and radio, historic sites, and digital media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded formats include public exhibitions, broadcast documentaries, large-scale public-facing digital projects, and programs designed for broad public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division: Division of Research priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Research makes awards to support the publication of books in and outside the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes support for scholarly book projects and related research dissemination activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division: Division of Education priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Education works to support and strengthen teaching of the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs under this division target curricular development, teacher training, materials for classrooms, and other education-focused initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Federal/State Partnership priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Federal/State Partnership collaborates with 56 state and territory humanities councils to strengthen local programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This office focuses on supporting and coordinating local/state-level humanities programming through the network of councils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Digital Humanities priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Digital Humanities advises on use of technology in the humanities and coordinates digital humanities activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priorities include projects that use or advance digital methods, tools, infrastructure, and scholarship in the humanities (office established in 2008).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special initiative: Bridging Cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Bridging Cultures was an initiative that explored ways the humanities promote understanding and mutual respect for people with diverse histories, cultures, and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects supported through this initiative focused on cultures globally as well as within the United States and prioritized intercultural understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special initiative: Standing Together
rubrics_metrics.description: Standing Together marks a priority to make awards that promote understanding of the military experience and to support returning veterans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This initiative prioritized projects about the military experience, veterans' perspectives, and civic understanding related to military service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special initiative: We the People
rubrics_metrics.description: We the People was a funding stream designed to encourage and enhance the teaching, study, and understanding of American history, culture, and democratic principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initiative supported projects that explore significant events and themes in the nation's history and that advance knowledge of principles that define America; it ran as a chair-directed priority (active 2002–2009 and described as inspiring a renaissance in knowledge about American history).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jefferson Lecture selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jefferson Lecture 'recognizes an individual who has made significant scholarly contributions in the humanities and who has the ability to communicate the knowledge and wisdom of the humanities in a broadly appealing way.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Jefferson Lecturer is selected each year by the National Council on the Humanities; award includes an honorarium and public lecture in Washington, D.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Humanities Medal criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Humanities Medal honors individuals or groups whose work has deepened the nation's understanding of the humanities, broadened citizens' engagement with the humanities, or helped preserve and expand Americans' access to important resources in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to 12 medals can be awarded each year; replaced the Charles Frankel Prize (1989–1996).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program vs. initiative distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Special initiatives are priorities of the Endowment that indicate critical areas identified by the NEH chair; they differ from the divisions in that they do not sponsor or coordinate specific grant programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction informs applicants whether an area is an ongoing program-managed funding stream (division) or a chair-priority emphasis (initiative) that may guide but not directly administer specific grant competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of fundable project types (illustrative precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable NEH-sponsored projects include museum exhibitions, large documentaries (e.g., Ken Burns' The Civil War), editorial/edition projects (Library of America), large-scale digitization and transcription projects, and scholarly conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples indicate the scale and public reach NEH has historically funded and can serve as precedents for the kinds of high-quality humanities projects the agency supports.
